properties.name: Every element of a design is a black box with inner function and interfaces, nested as deep as the design needs, in any domain
properties.statement:
Anthony, 2026-08-07, in his words: treat everything in design as a systems-engineering BLACK BOX that has some inner functionality and an interface with other black boxes. Inside a black box may be a series of other black boxes making up the parent black box, and this continues down further and further as the design needs — system-of-systems level, then systems level, then component level, and so on. This should apply to just about any design project, from code projects to biology projects. Secondly, graph theory is then applied over which functions are allocated to which systems.

HE ADDED, AND IT IS THE POINT OF RECORDING THIS: "I'm a little surprised that reflow2 does not have this as it was one of the primary things I designed it for." So this requirement is not new intent — it is ORIGINAL intent that had no node, which is the failure mode this project has hit before (dec:idea-backlog-belongs-in-the-graph: accepted, invisible, violated, re-announced as new). Two prior answers in that conversation told him the recursive model was largely absent, and that was WRONG; the measurement below is the correction.

WHAT ALREADY EXISTS, measured 2026-08-07 rather than recalled: the vocabulary is complete and the backbone is real. Component carries a `level` (48 at `component`, 8 at `subsystem`), CONTAINS nests Component inside Component (42 edges), ALLOCATED_TO puts capabilities on components (138 edges), and the graph-theory half is built and running — evaluate_allocation computes modularity, god-components and misplaced capabilities; cap:hierarchy checks decomposition levels; req:analyse-at-any-level already requires that any level be analysable on its own; req:decomposition-covers-its-parent already requires a decomposition to be checkable against what the parent held. DECOMPOSES exists as an edge type and is UNUSED (0 instances) because CONTAINS carries it.

WHERE IT FALLS SHORT OF THE STATEMENT, and all three are measured:
1. DEPTH IS TWO, not "as deep as the design needs". Project -> 8 subsystems -> 42 components, max depth 2, nothing above system-of-systems and nothing below component. The schema does not bound this; the population does. And 14 components are roots — 6 ordinary components sit outside every subsystem, so the tree is not even complete at the depth it has.
2. THE INTERFACE HALF IS ~9% POPULATED. 5 Interface nodes and 5 PROVIDES / 5 CONSUMES edges for 56 components. "An interface with other black boxes" is the half that makes a black box a black box, and it is almost entirely unmodelled — the same fact the trajectory reports as `seams 0% (0/73)`.
3. THE DOMAIN CLAIM IS UNTESTED OUTSIDE SOFTWARE. Every calibration number behind the granularity guidance comes from code (110k LOC -> ~78 nodes; reflow2's own 34k LOC -> ~100 nodes). The adopt skill does explicitly claim non-code subjects and carries a table for them, but nothing has exercised "code projects to biology projects".

THE ASYMMETRY THIS EXPOSES, offered as reasoning rather than as settled: the standing guidance is one Interface per contract and one Artifact per meaningful unit, never per endpoint, file or function. For software that is defensible because the fine grain is REDUNDANTLY AVAILABLE — a compiler, an LSP and a type checker each hold element-level truth exactly and continuously, so a graph copy would be worse and staler. For a building, a satellite or an organism there is no compiler: nothing else holds "this penetration weakens this member", so the fine grain is not redundant, it is the only copy. The same rule may therefore be right for code and wrong for physical design, and reflow2 applies it uniformly.

WHAT WOULD SATISFY THIS, so it is not read as satisfied by the vocabulary alone: an arbitrary-depth nesting that is exercised beyond two levels, both sides of every contract modelled at each level so a change at one level propagates across siblings at that level (the electrical-drawing-affects-structural case he gave), and the allocation analysis reading something other than a perfect score over an empty structure.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
SHARPENED 2026-08-12 — THE CROSS-GRAPH READING, WHICH NOBODY HAD DRAWN OUT
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

Anthony, working the linking trial: "kind of getting to a place where we can do a bottoms-up approach of systems engineering where your system or system-of-systems is the composition of a bunch of independently developed and linked, but are federated, reflow2 projects that are the components or systems of the higher level project."

⭐ THIS REQUIREMENT HAS TWO READINGS AND ONLY ONE HAS EVER BEEN CONSIDERED.

  WITHIN A GRAPH — Component CONTAINS Component, `level`, matryoshka. This is what the statement above is about, and reflow2 already models itself as 8 `sys:*` components over 45 components.

  ACROSS GRAPHS — a WHOLE DESIGN, separately owned and independently developed, is a black box in a larger system. Same recursion, one level up, at an OWNERSHIP boundary rather than a containment one. Nothing in this requirement or its measurement addressed this, and it is what his framing adds.

⭐⭐ AND THE CROSS-GRAPH BLACK BOX ALREADY EXISTS — MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED. A mirror of flo2's published surface into a scratch reflow2 graph (2026-08-12, first time `mirror_surface` was run on a real pair) brought in 13 nodes: 1 Project, 6 Components, 5 Interfaces, 1 Artifact — with **5 CONTAINS edges from `proj:flo2`** plus PROVIDES/CONSUMES/SPECIFIES. So a mirrored design lands as A PROJECT NODE CONTAINING ITS PARTS, with its published interfaces as the ports: structurally a black box with an interface, sitting alongside the host design's own. The SHAPE this requirement asks for is therefore present across graphs as well as within one. What is absent is that NOTHING ASKS whether the thing just mirrored is a system in a larger one, and NO ANALYSIS RECURSES across that boundary.

⚠️ TOP-DOWN AND BOTTOM-UP ARE DIFFERENT PROBLEMS, and only the first was ever designed for. `req:one-design-or-several-is-asked` records reflow's S-04-decision — the System-of-Systems question asked BEFORE anything is built, which decomposes a concept into N designs, one directory each. That is TOP-DOWN: one owner, coordinated ids, boundaries designed together, released together. Anthony is describing BOTTOM-UP: N designs that already exist independently, from which the SoS emerges by linking.

EVERY GAP THE 2026-08-12 LINKING TRIAL FOUND IS A BOTTOM-UP GAP, and top-down composition would have had none of them:
  - ids are uncoordinated, so correspondence falls back on fuzzy names that re-guess every run;
  - boundaries were never agreed, so flo2 models reflow2 as a component it CONTAINS and pairing has no boundary to pair across;
  - release cadences differ by construction, so every comparison carries a version skew nothing discloses;
  - labelling is a bilateral precondition neither party gets value from until both have paid — which is why the whole linking layer has ZERO INSTANCES in either graph.

🛑 TWO THINGS BLOCK THE BOTTOM-UP READING, both concrete:
  (1) NO REFRESH. Found 2026-08-12 by running `mirror_surface` TWICE. The second mirror of the SAME design collided with itself — 12 of 13 ids refused as collisions, `mirrored_edges: 0`, `mirror_content_hash: null` — leaving the STALE node in place with the host's own CONSUMES edge still pointing at it, while `mirrors` continued to report the FIRST hash. So the staleness register reads FRESH after a failed refresh, which is worse than never refreshing. Re-mirroring one `mirror_of` is a DIFFERENT OPERATION from mirroring a new design ("replace what I hold of theirs at a new pin" versus "add a stranger and refuse clashes"), and only the second is implemented. A federation of independently-moving projects is MADE OF refreshes.
  (2) THE SoS-LEVEL INSTRUMENTS REPORT GREEN OVER EMPTINESS. `graph_report` says "Modularity 1.00 across 45 components; 0 misplaced", and `fact:defect-allocation-health-is-green-over-an-empty-structure` already records that this is computed over almost no dependencies. At system-of-systems level that is the `unmet_needs: 0` failure again — a confident number over an unpopulated structure — and this requirement's own closing line already demands "the allocation analysis reading something other than a perfect score over an empty structure".

📌 WHAT THIS DOES NOT CHANGE: `dec:nested-graphs` already settled that separately-owned designs are SEPARATE GRAPHS linked by mirroring, so the architecture for the cross-graph reading is decided and this is not a proposal to revisit it. What is added here is that the recursion this requirement asks for and that decision's composition mechanism ARE THE SAME THING at different scales, which neither node says.
